messages:
maya: customer reports structured-output parse failure when using json_mode. They posted a payload with JS-style comments + trailing commas; pydantic and zod both fail. Need triage.

support-bot: created INC-2026 and attached customer logs.

eli: can you paste the minimal repro?

maya: posting the snippet they sent (sanitized here):
```json
{
  "id": 42, // record id
  "name": "Widget",
  "tags": ["alpha", "beta",], /* trailing comma + comment */
}
```

maya: api build v2.4.1, runtime: hosted, mode: json_mode, model: open-llm-13b, request id: r-0a1b2c

raj: i repro locally feeding same payload via curl. pydantic raises: 
```
pydantic.json_schema.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 3 column 15 (char 42)
```

zoe: zod client sees: 
```
ZodError: Unexpected token / in JSON at position 24
```

eli: looks like non-strict JSON (comments/trailing commas). json_mode expects strict JSON by default. do we have a sanitizer option to strip comments?

maya: customer says other parsers (json5) accept it. they want Redwood to either accept json5-ish inputs or at least surface clearer errors pointing to comments/trailing commas.

raj: quick workaround: client-side preproc to remove comments/trailing commas. server-side we could add an opt-in sanitizer (enable_json5: true) that normalizes before parsing, but that risks masking schema drift.

zoe: UX improvement suggestion: change error mapping to something like "Invalid JSON: unrecognized token at line X. If payload contains comments or trailing commas, try removing them or enable 'json5' relax mode with header X-Redwood-Allow-Json5."

eli: technically we can implement a soft fallback: try strict parse -> on failure run a safe sanitizer that only strips line/block comments and trailing commas and reparse. always log fallback and set telemetry tag sanitized_input=true. that keeps visibility.

maya: customer asked for ETA. can support provide timeline?

support-bot: INC-2026 assigned to eng-ml (raj) + eng-runtime (eli).

raj: i'll prototype sanitizer today. need eng-runtime signoff for the runtime change. if ok, ship as opt-in header X-Redwood-Allow-Json5 in a hotfix.

eli: note streaming/json_mode interacts with our buffering. sanitizer must run before streaming tokenization. it will add ~2-5ms on payloads that contain comments. acceptable for most cases but note perf impact.

zoe: add integration tests: strict-pydantic path + sanitized path + telemetry assertions. also update docs with explicit note about json5-like payloads.

maya: customer is fine with an opt-in header for now. promised ETA ~2 business days for a prototype.

raj: created branch github.com/redwood/inference/issue/INC-2026-json5-sanitizer

eli: pushed initial unit tests and a small sanitizer util. sending repro curl for QA:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c" \
 -d '{ "input": { "id": 42, // comment } }'
```

maya: thanks — updated customer: opt-in header path + ETA ~2d. will reopen if they hit anything else. :thumbsup:

zoe: note for docs team: add a short note under structured-output -> "JSON5-like inputs (comments/trailing commas)" and document opt-in header + telemetry.

eli: i'll open PR once CI green.

raj: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/345 — awaiting review.

maya: marking resolved from customer side for now; will follow up on PR.
